title: Football transfer rumours: Everton to sign Barcelona's Yerry Mina?
trail: N’Golo Kanté to PSG? | Willian to Barcelona? | André Gomes to Arsenal? | Xherdan Shaqiri to Manchester United? Jack Wilshere to West Ham?
body: Everton have giant ambitions in this summer’s transfer market, the giant in question being England-bothering 6ft5in centre half Yerry Mina. Barcelona want to replace him with Sevilla’s Clément Lenglet – whose current club’s director of football, Joaquín Caparrós, insisted yesterday that the Frenchman was going nowhere unless someone meets his £26.5m release clause in full – and are prepared to cash in on Mina’s eye-catching performances at the World Cup with Colombia, with the Liverpool Echo reporting that Everton have, like one of his international team-mates with Jordan Henderson’s chin, “already made contact”. Real Madrid say the idea of them paying £240m for Kylian Mbappé is “completely false” because they “have not made any offer” and furthermore “condemn the spreading of this kind of information”. So that’s that sorted. Barcelona might buy Willian, whose agent, Kia Joorabchian, has been in the city this week and who is apparently so desperate to play alongside Lionel Messi that he will snub an alternative offer from Manchester United. Barcelona will look to bring the cash value of the deal down by offering any of André Gomes, Rafinha or Paulinho in part-exchange. This will come as a surprise and a disappointment to Arsenal, who want André Gomes themselves and are willing to pay as much as £30m for him, according to the Independent. Paris St-Germain have only just signed Mbappé themselves, but they have not finished their summer spending. L’Equipe report that at a meeting this week to discuss their transfer ambitions the club’s sporting director, Antero Henrique, announced his intention to purchase a top-level left-back, with the names of David Alba and Alex Sandro mentioned, but revealed that his absolutely toppermost target was Chelsea’s N’Golo Kanté, and expects that he will be available for £90m. Jack Butland’s pay packet at Stoke is about to get an unusual post-relegation twist – as his salary goes up by £20,000 a week. The Potters are worried that Chelsea or Liverpool might swoop for their trusted English shot-stopper, and have thus slapped a £30m price tag upon his gloves and will endeavour to get him to sign a new, improved contract. But if he stays Xherdan Shaqiri is unlikely to be there with him, with the Sun saying that José Mourinho has been impressed by his performances at the World Cup and that Manchester United might now join the queue of clubs lining up to trigger his £12m release clause. Mourinho is also keen on Mario Mandzukic, and could hand Juventus their long-term target Matteo Darmian to land him in a swap arrangement. Jack Wilshere has held talks with West Ham and, although other Premier League clubs including Wolves and Everton are reportedly interested, seems set to choose between the Hammers and a very different and very lucrative experience at Fenerbahce. The Hammers are also one of two clubs, the other being Burnley, to have had an offer turned down by West Brom for Craig Dawson, prompting the player to hand in a transfer request. Ben Foster, similarly keen on leaving the Hawthorns, is near a £4m move to Watford. Liverpool fans will meanwhile be astonished when they learn the identity of the goalkeeper Jürgen Klopp intends to put his faith in next season – it’s Loris Karius, the Champions League calamity-magnet himself. Moves for Jan Oblak and Alisson have been deemed too expensive, and Klopp is reported by the Mirror to have “zero interest” in Barcelona’s Jasper Cillessen, Leicester’s Kasper Schmeichel, Lazio’s Thomas Strakosha and Werder Bremen’s Jiri Pavlenka, who have all been linked with moves to Anfield. They might however sign a young right-back, with the 16-year-old Ajax prodigy Ki-Jana Hoever currently training on Merseyside.
